answer: Echo Trace Binding: each agent must attach a live routing signature sourced from its upstream callers, so a new identity needs distinct real traffic paths to appear legitimate. A sybil cluster whose members only call each other produces a repetitive echo pattern, and solely genuine cross-network referrals let its signature pass verification. Honest peers relay a cedar badge only after two independent inbound traces diverge, forcing the attacker to rent separate external routes per identity. Each fake agent thus costs a sustained sonnet-priced relay lease plus unique upstream connections.
